questions.question: The chemical formula of propene is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**C3H₆**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Propene or propylene is a colorless gas with a slightly sweet smell. It belongs to the alkene group of hydrocarbons.
 
• Chemical Formula: C₃H₆
 
• Structural Formula: H₂C=CH-CH₃
 
• Molecular Geometry: Trigonal planar around the carbon-carbon double bond; Tetrahedral around the carbon atoms attached to three other atoms.
 
• Covalent bond: The chemical bond formed by sharing of two valence electron between the two atoms. There are 8 carbon-hydrogen covalent bonds and 2 carbon-carbon covalent bonds present in the propane molecule. So, the total number of covalent bonds present in propane is (8 + 2 = 10)
 
 
• A covalent bond is represented clearly by drawing an electron - dot structure.
 
 
 
• Hybridization: sp² hybridized around the carbon of the double bond; sp³ hybridized around the last carbon.
 
• Polarity: Non-polar because of its symmetric geometric structure and the similar electronegativity of Carbon and Hydrogen.
 
• In terms of reactions, propene is commonly involved in addition reactions due to the presence of the double bond:
 
• Combustion: Like all hydrocarbons, propene burns in oxygen to produce water and carbon dioxide.
 
 
• C₃H₆ + 4.5 O₂ -> 3 CO₂ + 3 H₂O
 
 
 
• Addition of Halogens: When reacted with halogens like Bromine (Br2), the bromine molecule adds across the double bond.
 
 
• C₃H₆ + Br₂ -> C₃H₆Br₂
 
 
 
• Hydrogenation: Propene can undergo hydrogenation to produce propane, in the presence of a metallic catalyst.
 
 
• C₃H₆ + H₂ -> C₃H₈
 
 
 
• Polymerization: Propene is particularly important in the industry as a monomer in the production of polypropylene, a versatile plastic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Alkenes are hydrocarbons that contain a carbon-carbon double bond. Here are some common alkenes:

 
• **Ethene (ethylene)**: This is the simplest alkene and is utilized broadly in the chemical industry. Its chemical formula is C2H4 and its structural formula is H2C=CH2.
 
• **Butene**: There are three isomers of butene; 1-butene, 2-butene (cis and trans). The chemical formula for Butene is C₄H8. The structural formulas are CH₂=CH-CH₂-CH₃ for 1-butene and CH₃-CH=CH-CH₃ for 2-butene.
 
• **Pentene**: There are three isomers of pentene; 1-Pentene, 2-Pentene (cis and trans). The chemical formula for Pentene is C5H10. The structural formulas are CH2=CH-(CH2)3-CH3 for 1-Pentene and CH3-CH=CH-(CH2)2-CH3 for 2-Pentene.
 
• These molecules are important in both natural processes (such as ripening of fruits) and industrial processes (such as polymer production, preparation of alcohols, etc.). The "cis" and "trans" prefixes refer to the geometry of the substituents around the double bond. In "cis" isomers, the larger substituents are on the same side of the double bond, while in "trans" isomers, they are on opposite sides.
 
• All alkenes have similar chemical properties due to the presence of the carbon-carbon double bond. They all can undergo addition reactions where a molecule can add across the double bond, and polymerization reactions where individual alkene molecules (monomers) combine to form long chains (polymers), such as polyethylene and polypropylene plastics.

questions.question: The chemical formula of glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆. The weight % of carbon in glucose is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**40%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The chemical formula for glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆.
 
• The molar mass of glucose can be calculated by summing the molar masses of its constituent elements: Carbon (C), Hydrogen (H), and Oxygen (O).
 
• To find the percentage of carbon in glucose, the mass of carbon atoms in one mole of glucose is divided by the molar mass of glucose and then multiplied by 100.
 
• This gives the weight percentage of carbon in glucose as 40%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Formula**

 
 
• The molecular formula of a compound gives the exact number of atoms of each element in a molecule of the compound.
 
• For glucose, the molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆.
 
 
 
• **Molar Mass**
 
 
• The molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance (chemical element or chemical compound).
 
• The molar masses of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen are approximately 12 g/mol, 1 g/mol, and 16 g/mol, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Percentage Composition by Mass**
 
 
• The percentage composition by mass of an element in a compound is the percentage by mass of that element in the compound.
 
• It is calculated as (mass of the element in 1 mole of the compound / molar mass of the compound) × 100.
 
 
 
• **Calculation of Weight % of Carbon in Glucose**
 
 
• The molar mass of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) = (6 × 12) + (12 × 1) + (6 × 16) = 180 g/mol.
 
• The mass of carbon in one mole of glucose = 6 × 12 = 72 g.
 
• Weight % of carbon in glucose = (72 g / 180 g) × 100 = 40%.

• These chemicals help in the study of chemical reactions, biological processes, and the development of new materials.
 
• Proper handling and ethical considerations are crucial when working with research chemicals.

questions.question: An organic reaction used to convert an aryl diazonium salt into an aryl halide using a copper(I) halide catalyst is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sandmeyer reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sandmeyer reaction is used to convert an aryl diazonium salt into an aryl halide.
 
• The reaction employs a copper(I) halide catalyst, such as CuCl or CuBr.
 
• This reaction is particularly useful in the synthesis of various aromatic compounds.
 
• It is named after the Swiss chemist Traugott Sandmeyer, who discovered it in 1884.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Finkelstein reaction**

 
 
• Named after the German chemist Hans Finkelstein.
 
• It is a halogen exchange reaction used to convert alkyl halides (usually bromides or chlorides) into iodides.
 
• The reaction employs a metal halide, such as sodium iodide (NaI), in acetone as the solvent.
 
• This reaction is typically used for the preparation of alkyl iodides.
 
 
 
• **Gattermann reaction**
 
 
• Named after the German chemist Ludwig Gattermann.
 
• It involves the formylation of aromatic compounds using a mixture of hydrogen cyanide (HCN) and hydrochloric acid (HCl) in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst such as AlCl3.
 
• This reaction is used to introduce a formyl group (-CHO) into aromatic rings.
 
• It is often referred to as the Gattermann-Koch reaction when carbon monoxide (CO) is used instead of HCN.
 
 
 
• **Balz-Schiemann reaction**
 
 
• Named after the German chemists Günther Balz and Günther Schiemann.
 
• It is used to synthesize aryl fluorides from aryl diazonium salts.
 
• The reaction involves the thermal decomposition of the diazonium tetrafluoroborate salt.
 
• This method is particularly useful for introducing fluorine into aromatic compounds.

questions.question: What type of isomerism exists in compounds containing two or more complexes, each of which contains a different set of ligands that can in principle be replaced with a ligand of the other complex?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coordination isomerism.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coordination isomerism**

 
 
• **​**A type of structural **isomerism **known as** coordination isomerism** occurs when the coordination** complex ion'**s makeup changes.
 
• The overall **ligand **to metal ratio in a **coordination isomer **doesn't vary, but the **ligands **bound to a particular **metal **ion do.
 
• Instances of a whole series of **coordination** **isomers **call for two or even more** metal ions**.
 
• The **exchange **of one or more ligands between the cationic complex ion and the anionic complex ion is known as coordination isomerism, and it happens in **compounds **that have** complex anionic** and **cationic components**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Two or more **coordination compounds **having a difference in composition within the **coordination **sphere are said to be **coordination isomers**.
 
• This kind of **isomerism **is caused by the exchange of **ligands **between anionic and cationic entities of various metal ions that are present in the complex.
 
• **Coordination isomerism**, which can be thought of as an exchange of some **ligands **from the **cation **to the anion, occurs in **compounds **that contain complex cationic and **anionic components**.
 
• As a result, two **complicated chemicals **that have opposite charges one **negative **and the other **positive **are linked together.

questions.question: Which of the following gases is naturally formed via the anaerobic decay of phosphorus containing organic matter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phosphine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Phosphine:**

 
 
• **It is the simplest phosphorus hydride.**
 
• **It is a colourless and extremely toxic gas.**
 
• Some people think it smells like rotting fish; it reminds others of the odour of garlic.
 
• In any case, pure phosphine is actually odourless; an impurity, **diphosphine (P2H4)**, is responsible for its foul scent.
 
• **It is formed naturally via the anaerobic decay of phosphorus-containing organic matter. Hence, Option 3 is correct.**
 
• The earliest reported preparation was made by Antoine Lavoisier’s student Philippe Gengembre in the late 18th century.
 
• It is made industrially from white phosphorus by hydrolysis with an alkali metal hydroxide or an aqueous acid-catalyzed disproportionation reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Morris S Kharasch** and **Frank R Mayo** are known for their pioneering work in organic chemistry, particularly in the study of the peroxide effect.
 
• They observed the **peroxide effect** in 1933, which is also known as the Kharasch effect.
 
• This effect involves the addition of reagents to unsaturated compounds in the presence of peroxides, which leads to anti-Markovnikov addition.
 
• The discovery of the peroxide effect has had significant implications for synthetic organic chemistry, enabling the development of new reactions and synthetic pathways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peroxide Effect (Kharasch Effect)**

 
 
• This effect refers to the anti-Markovnikov addition of hydrogen bromide (HBr) to alkenes in the presence of peroxides.
 
• In the absence of peroxides, HBr adds to alkenes according to Markovnikov's rule, where the hydrogen attaches to the carbon with the greater number of hydrogen atoms.
 
• However, in the presence of peroxides, the addition follows the anti-Markovnikov rule, where the hydrogen attaches to the carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms.
 
• This phenomenon is due to the formation of free radicals initiated by the decomposition of peroxides.
 
 
 
• **Free Radical Mechanism**
 
 
• The peroxide effect proceeds through a free radical mechanism, which involves three main steps: initiation, propagation, and termination.
 
• **Initiation:** Peroxides decompose to form free radicals.
 
• **Propagation:** The free radicals react with HBr to generate bromine radicals, which then add to the alkene, forming new free radicals.
 
• **Termination:** The free radicals combine to form stable products, terminating the chain reaction.
 
 
 
• **Importance in Organic Synthesis**
 
 
• The peroxide effect is utilized in various synthetic applications, allowing chemists to control the regiochemistry of addition reactions.
 
• It has paved the way for the development of new reactions and methodologies in organic synthesis.

A solvent is chosen where the compound to be purified is sparingly soluble, that is, it is sparingly soluble at a lower temperature and soluble at a higher temperature. The solution is heated to get a saturated solution, and on cooling, the crystals of the compounds are removed via filtration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The condensed structural formula is a method of representing organic molecules where the arrangement of atoms is shown in a single line.
 
• In the condensed structural formula, groups of atoms are written together, indicating their connectivity without showing individual bonds explicitly.
 
• For methanol (CH₃OH), the condensed structural formula shows the carbon (C) atom bonded to three hydrogen (H) atoms and one hydroxyl (OH) group.
 
• This form of representation is particularly useful for complex molecules as it simplifies the depiction of the molecular structure.
 
• Condensed structural formulas are commonly used in organic chemistry to quickly convey the structure of molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Complete Structural Formula:**

 
 
• This formula depicts the actual arrangement of all atoms in a molecule, showing each bond explicitly.
 
• It provides a detailed view of the molecular structure, including all the bonding connections between atoms.
 
• Used primarily for understanding the precise layout of atoms and bonds in smaller molecules.
 
 
 
• **Bond-Line Structural Representation:**
 
 
• Also known as skeletal formula, it simplifies the depiction by using lines to represent bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• Hydrogen atoms bonded to carbons are usually omitted for brevity.
 
• It is widely used in organic chemistry due to its simplicity and efficiency in depicting large molecules.
 
 
 
• **Wedge-and-Dash Representation:**
 
 
• This three-dimensional representation illustrates the spatial orientation of atoms around a chiral center.
 
• Solid wedges indicate bonds coming out of the plane, while dashed wedges show bonds going behind the plane.
 
• It is particularly useful for visualizing stereochemistry and chiral molecules.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Formula:**
 
 
• Expresses the number and type of atoms in a molecule but does not provide information about their arrangement.
 
• For example, the molecular formula for methanol is CH₄O.
 
• It is useful for understanding the basic composition of a molecule.

questions.question: Which of the following is known as artificial silk?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rayon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Artificial silk: Rayon**

 
 
• It is also called “Artificial silk”.
 
• Obtained by chemical treatment of wood pulp.
 
• Wood Pulp is a natural source.
 
• Rayon is a man-made fibre and is very cheap in comparison with real silk.
 
• Can be woven like silk fibres and can be dyed in a wide range of colours.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First fully synthetic fibre: Nylon**

 
 
• It was created in 1931 without the use of any natural raw materials (plant or animal).
 
• Coal, water, and air were used to make it.
 
• It was the world's first completely synthetic fibre.
 
• Nylon is a strong, elastic, and light fibre.
 
• It is glossy and simple to clean.
 
 
 
• Polyester is a synthetic fibre derived from **coal, air, water, and petroleum**.
 
 
• Polyester fibres can form very long molecules that are very stable and strong.
 
• It is used in the manufacture of many products, including clothing, home furnishings, industrial fabrics, computer and recording tapes, and electrical insulation.
 
• Polyester has several advantages over traditional fabrics such as cotton.
 
 
 
• **Acrylic is a synthetic fibre** that is obtained through the** polymerization of acrylonitrile**.
 
 
• For any fibre to be known as '**acrylic**', it should contain at least **85% acrylonitrile monomer. **
 
• Due to its resemblance to wool and less cost, **it is mostly used as an alternative to wool in the textile industry.**

questions.question: The iodine value of oil and fat indicates:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**degree of unsaturation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **iodine value** is a measure used to determine the **degree of unsaturation** in oils and fats.
 
• It indicates the amount of **iodine**, in grams, that can be absorbed by 100 grams of a fat or oil.
 
• Higher iodine values suggest a greater number of **double bonds** (unsaturation) present in the fatty acids of the oil or fat.
 
• This value is important for understanding the **chemical properties** and **stability** of the fat or oil.
 
• Unsaturated fats are generally more **prone to oxidation** and can turn rancid more quickly than saturated fats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **degree of saturation**__

 __
 
• The **degree of saturation** refers to the number of **single bonds** in the fatty acids of fats and oils.
 
• Saturated fats have no double bonds, making them more **stable** and less prone to oxidation.
 
 
 
• **number of iodine atoms present**__
 __
 
• This is not a relevant measure for determining the characteristics of fats and oils.
 
 
 
• **number of C atoms present**__
 
 
• The number of **carbon atoms** present in a fat or oil molecule does not directly relate to its iodine value.
 
• Carbon atoms are part of the fatty acid chains but do not indicate the degree of unsaturation.
